newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Macedonian students stage separate demonstrations.
newsitem.headline: Macedonian students stage separate demonstrations.

text.p: Students in Macedonia staged two demonstrations on Friday, one opposing a plan to use Albanian as a second language at a teaching institution and the other seeking recognition for an illegal Albanian university.

Several hundred students protested against a government decision to hold classes at the Paedagogical Academy in Skopje in the Albanian language. With rare exceptions, Macedonian is now the only language for higher studies.
In Tetovo, several hundred ethnic Albanian students demonstrated to demand that the government legalise the Albanian university in Tetovo and release its rector, Dr Fadil Sulejmani, from prison.
The university, which is not recognised by the government, was set up two years ago by Albanian intellectuals after the authorities closed the Albanian university in Pristina.
The Macedonia branch of the Helsinki Committee for Human Rights issued a statement criticising the government's educational policy.

It said the government did not have "a clear attitude towards the problems in higher education that provoke student demonstrations of all nationalities and generate political manipulations and inter-ethnic tensions."
Ethnic Albanians made up 23 percent of Macedonia's population of two million, according to a 1994 census in the former Yugoslav republic.
